issues.legal_issue: A ceiling case may be reopened when the required notice is issued within the applicable limitation period and satisfies the statutory requirements.
material_facts: An earlier ceiling order dropped the proceedings in 1972.
The State produced a notice dated 20 November 1976, issued within five years of that order.
The Court found that the notice met the requirements for reopening the case.
issues.conclusion: The reopening was within the limitation period, and this issue was decided in favour of the State.
issues.legal_principle: Section 15 of the Rajasthan Imposition of Ceiling on Agricultural Holdings Act, 1973 permits reopening in the circumstances specified there, subject to a show-cause notice and the proviso barring notice after the later of five years from the final order or 30 June 1979. The relevant dates are the date of the order sought to be reopened and the date the notice was issued. No earlier case was relied on.

predicates.ceiling_case_reopening_proceeding: A public authority sought to reopen an earlier order in a land-ceiling case.
predicates.notice_within_applicable_deadline: The authority issued the reopening notice within the applicable time limit measured from the earlier order and the statutory outer date.
predicates.notice_met_reopening_requirements: The reopening notice satisfied the requirements applicable to such a notice.

issues.definition: If a ceiling case is being reopened and the notice is timely and compliant, the reopening is timely.

issues.legal_issue: A gift of immovable property is valid when the required formalities are met and the donee accepts it during the donor’s lifetime, which may be inferred from conduct and surrounding circumstances.
material_facts: The donor executed a registered gift deed signed by him and attested by two witnesses.
The deed stated that ownership and possession were being transferred immediately and that the donee could cultivate the land.
Revenue records recorded the gift in the donee’s favour.
The donor and donee stated that the donee possessed and cultivated the land after the gift; the donee was an adult and lived separately.
The State produced no evidence rebutting the donee’s enjoyment of the property.
issues.conclusion: The donee accepted the gift by conduct during the donor’s lifetime, the statutory formalities were satisfied, and the gift was valid.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 122 and 123 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 require a voluntary, gratuitous gift accepted during the donor’s lifetime and, for immovable property, a registered instrument signed by or on behalf of the donor and attested by at least two witnesses. Section 122 prescribes no particular mode of acceptance; acceptance may be inferred from surrounding circumstances, including delivery of the deed or possession. The Court relied on Naramadaben Maganlal Thakker v. Pranjivandas Maganlal Thakker, (1997) 2 SCC 255, and Asokan v. Lakshmikutty, (2007) 13 SCC 210.

rule.if: land_ceiling_proceeding and gift_formalities_met and acceptance_during_donors_lifetime and (gift_deed_indicated_immediate_transfer or donee_possessed_or_cultivated_property)

predicates.land_ceiling_proceeding: An authority determined whether land was available for resumption in a ceiling case.
predicates.gift_formalities_met: The donor made a voluntary gift of immovable property through a registered instrument signed by the donor and attested by two witnesses.
predicates.acceptance_during_donors_lifetime: The donee received the gift, expressly or by conduct, while the donor was alive and capable of giving.
predicates.gift_deed_indicated_immediate_transfer: The gift deed stated that ownership or possession was to pass to the donee immediately.
predicates.donee_possessed_or_cultivated_property: The donee took possession of or cultivated the gifted property.

issues.definition: When a ceiling case concerns a gift of immovable property, the gift is valid if its formalities are met and the donee accepts it during the donor’s lifetime, as shown by immediate-transfer terms or the donee’s possession or cultivation.

issues.legal_issue: A transfer qualifying for the statutory exception to the general rule against recognizing certain land transfers must be excluded from ceiling calculations, even if the general rule would otherwise apply.
material_facts: The donor was an agriculturist and transferred land to his adult son, who was capable of cultivating land personally and intended to pursue agriculture.
The son possessed and cultivated the land, had agricultural equipment, and supported himself as an agriculturist.
The transfer was made before the statutory cutoff and covered less than the maximum area recognized by the exception.
The gift deed and the statements of the donor and son supported the transfer and its agricultural purpose.
issues.conclusion: The transfer qualified for the exception and was protected from the general restriction; the transferred land was not to be included in calculating confiscable surplus land.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 30C and 30D of the Rajasthan Tenancy Act, 1955 set the ceiling area and generally disregard specified voluntary transfers. Section 30DD, which begins with a non-obstante clause, recognizes qualifying transfers made within its stated area and time limits to an agriculturist’s son or brother who meets the specified agricultural and age conditions. A transfer within that exception is protected notwithstanding Section 30D. No earlier case was relied on.

rule.if: land_ceiling_proceeding and transfer_to_eligible_agricultural_son and transferee_capable_and_intending_to_farm and transferee_adult_by_required_time and transfer_area_within_permitted_limit and transfer_before_eligibility_cutoff

predicates.land_ceiling_proceeding: An authority determined whether land was available for resumption in a ceiling case.
predicates.transfer_to_eligible_agricultural_son: A landholder transferred land to a son who met the applicable agricultural eligibility conditions.
predicates.transferee_capable_and_intending_to_farm: The transferee was capable of cultivating land personally and intended to pursue agriculture.
predicates.transferee_adult_by_required_time: The transferee had attained majority by the time required for the exception.
predicates.transfer_area_within_permitted_limit: The area transferred did not exceed the maximum area recognized by the exception.
predicates.transfer_before_eligibility_cutoff: The transfer was made before the cutoff applicable to the exception.

issues.definition: In a ceiling case, a transfer to an eligible agricultural son is excluded from ceiling calculations if the transferee is capable of and intends to farm, has attained majority by the required time, and the transfer meets the applicable area and cutoff conditions.

issues.legal_issue: A later ceiling-law provision deeming specified transfers to defeat the law does not apply to an earlier bona fide transfer where the earlier ceiling regime governs the reopened case.
material_facts: The land was transferred by gift in 1963, before the period covered by the later law’s deeming provision.
The reopened case was decided under the earlier tenancy-law ceiling provisions, and the repeal of those provisions was not retrospective.
The Court found no evidence that the gift was actuated by extraneous consideration and treated it as bona fide.
issues.conclusion: The later ceiling-law provision did not affect the transfer, which was a bona fide transfer made before the provision’s specified period.
issues.legal_principle: Section 40 of the Rajasthan Imposition of Ceiling on Agricultural Holdings Act, 1973 repealed the relevant chapter of the Rajasthan Tenancy Act, 1955 without retrospective effect. Section 6 of the 1973 Act applies its deeming rule to transfers made within the period specified there; it does not capture a transfer made before that period. The Court also noted that bona fide transfers not actuated by extraneous consideration are exempt from that rule. No earlier case was relied on.

rule.if: land_ceiling_proceeding and case_governed_by_earlier_ceiling_regime and transfer_predates_later_law_trigger_period and transfer_is_bona_fide

predicates.land_ceiling_proceeding: An authority determined whether land was available for resumption in a ceiling case.
predicates.case_governed_by_earlier_ceiling_regime: The reopened case was decided under the ceiling rules that applied before the later law took effect.
predicates.transfer_predates_later_law_trigger_peri: The transfer occurred before the period to which the later law’s transfer-deeming rule applies.
predicates.transfer_is_bona_fide: The transfer was genuine and was not shown to have been made for an extraneous or evasive purpose.

issues.definition: When an earlier ceiling regime governs a case, a bona fide transfer made before the later law’s trigger period is not affected by that later transfer bar.
